libra.title: Libra
libra.author: Don DeLillo
libra.why: DeLillo's fictional take on Lee Harvey Oswald and the Kennedy assassination; readers who liked White Noise seek it out.

colour of magic.title: The Colour of Magic
colour of magic.author: Terry Pratchett
colour of magic.why: The first Discworld novel, a madcap parody of fantasy; fans enjoy it though many suggest starting elsewhere in the series.

gardens of the moon.title: Gardens of the Moon
gardens of the moon.author: Steven Erikson
gardens of the moon.why: The dense, unexplained start of the Malazan series; recommended as straight-up swords and magic for patient fantasy fans.

spirit catches you and you fall down.title: The Spirit Catches You and You Fall Down
spirit catches you and you fall down.author: Anne Fadiman
spirit catches you and you fall down.why: A Hmong child's epilepsy shows the clash between American medicine and her family's beliefs; readers remember it long after.

dies the fire.title: Dies the fire
dies the fire.author: S. M. Stirling
dies the fire.why: All technology suddenly stops working and survivors in Oregon fight to rebuild; an engaging post-apocalyptic start to a series.

matilda.title: Matilda
matilda.author: Roald Dahl
matilda.why: Dahl's story of a clever girl with telekinetic powers and awful grown-ups; a beloved childhood read.

institute.title: The Institute
institute.author: Stephen King
institute.why: Kids with special abilities are held in a secret facility; a gripping King thriller one reader finished in a weekend.

nightbitch.title: Nightbitch
nightbitch.author: Rachel Yoder
nightbitch.why: A stay-at-home mother believes she is turning into a dog; readers see it as a sharp metaphor for motherhood.

gates of fire.title: Gates of fire
gates of fire.author: Steven Pressfield
gates of fire.why: A fictional telling of the Battle of Thermopylae from a Spartan squire's view; readers say it moved them deeply.

perfect marriage.title: The Perfect Marriage
perfect marriage.author: Jeneva Rose
perfect marriage.why: A lawyer defends her husband accused of murder in this twisty thriller; readers wish they could read it fresh again.

looking for alaska.title: Looking for Alaska
looking for alaska.author: John Green
looking for alaska.why: Comments are split and one reader felt nothing about it; not clearly recommended.

warbreaker.title: Warbreaker
warbreaker.author: Brandon Sanderson
warbreaker.why: Readers split and one calls it bad on many levels; not clearly recommended.

whalefall.title: Whalefall
whalefall.author: Daniel Kraus
whalefall.why: A young man is swallowed by a sperm whale and must survive inside it; NPR-endorsed, gripping and surprisingly emotional.

my cousin rachel.title: My Cousin Rachel
my cousin rachel.author: Daphne du Maurier
my cousin rachel.why: Du Maurier's novel about whether a widow is a murderer or an innocent; readers love its ambiguity.

outer dark.title: Outer Dark
outer dark.author: Cormac McCarthy
outer dark.why: McCarthy's early grim, Gothic tale of a brother and sister in the rural South; bleak and powerful.

broken country.title: Broken Country
broken country.author: Clare Leslie Hall
broken country.why: A farmer's wife is torn between husband and an old love in post-war England; readers say it is moving and unputdownable.

dark places.title: Dark Places
dark places.author: Gillian Flynn
dark places.why: Readers disagree and one found the ending ridiculous; not clearly recommended.

rook.title: The Rook
rook.author: Daniel O'Malley
rook.why: An amnesiac woman discovers she runs a secret supernatural agency in Britain; a quirky, fun ride.

heroes die.title: Heroes die
heroes die.author: Matthew Woodring Stover
heroes die.why: Readers split, one calling its concept tired and overwritten; not clearly recommended.

zombie.title: Zombie
zombie.author: Joyce Carol Oates
zombie.why: Comments recommend other zombie-titled books, not Oates's novel; the entry does not match the discussion.

eragon.title: Eragon
eragon.author: Christopher Paolini
eragon.why: A farm boy finds a dragon egg in the first Inheritance Cycle book; an easy fantasy adventure for young readers.

power of now.title: The Power of Now
power of now.author: Eckhart Tolle
power of now.why: Tolle's guide to living in the present; readers say it changed their lives and helped them stop overthinking.

shadow of the gods.title: The Shadow of the Gods
shadow of the gods.author: John Gwynne
shadow of the gods.why: Readers split between a favourite and a book with dull characters; not clearly recommended.

letters to a young poet.title: Letters to a young poet
letters to a young poet.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
letters to a young poet.why: Rilke's ten letters of advice to a young writer on solitude and creating; readers find it timeless and inspiring.

erasure.title: Erasure
erasure.author: Percival L. Everett
erasure.why: A frustrated Black novelist writes a parody that becomes a hit; a sharp satire on publishing and race.

testaments.title: The Testaments
testaments.author: Margaret Atwood
testaments.why: Atwood's sequel to The Handmaid's Tale told by three women inside Gilead; recommended as gripping dystopian fiction.

bibliophobia.title: Bibliophobia
bibliophobia.author: Sarah Chihaya
bibliophobia.why: A book of personal essays about how reading changes our lives, recommended for writers of memoir.

salt.title: Salt
salt.author: Adam Roberts
salt.why: Roberts's early science fiction about two colonies on a salt planet at war; a reader enjoyed it.

nothing to envy.title: Nothing to envy
nothing to envy.author: Barbara Demick
nothing to envy.why: Stories of ordinary North Koreans; reads like gripping fiction and gives a rare look at daily life.

peace like a river.title: Peace like a river
peace like a river.author: Leif Enger
peace like a river.why: A boy narrates his family's flight across the Midwest after his brother is accused of murder; loved for its prose.

tin drum.title: The Tin Drum
tin drum.author: Gunter Grass
tin drum.why: Readers split, and one lists it among books they gave up on; not clearly recommended.

beautiful ugly.title: Beautiful Ugly
beautiful ugly.author: Alice Feeney
beautiful ugly.why: One reader calls it terrible but readable; not a clear recommendation.

elegance of the hedgehog.title: The Elegance of the Hedgehog
elegance of the hedgehog.author: Muriel Barbery
elegance of the hedgehog.why: A concierge and a precocious girl find beauty in a Paris building; a gentle book about hidden depths.

glorious exploits.title: Glorious Exploits
glorious exploits.author: Ferdia Lennon
glorious exploits.why: Two potters in Syracuse stage Greek plays with Athenian prisoners; praised as funny, moving and unusual.

centennial.title: Centennial
centennial.author: James A. Michener
centennial.why: Michener's sprawling saga of a Colorado town across centuries, rooted in geology and history.

space between worlds.title: The Space Between Worlds
space between worlds.author: Micaiah Johnson
space between worlds.why: A woman travels between parallel Earths where her other selves are dead; recommended along with its sequel.

atomic habits.title: Atomic Habits
atomic habits.author: James Clear
atomic habits.why: James Clear's practical book on forming good habits through small changes; recommended even by self-help sceptics.

brooklyn.title: Brooklyn
brooklyn.author: Colm Tóibín
brooklyn.why: An Irish girl emigrates to 1950s Brooklyn and must choose between two homes; a quiet, moving novel.

dirty job.title: A Dirty Job
dirty job.author: Christopher Moore
dirty job.why: A beta male becomes a death merchant in San Francisco; a comic fantasy readers say made them laugh hard.

confessions of a prairie bitch.title: Confessions of a prairie bitch
confessions of a prairie bitch.author: Alison Arngrim
confessions of a prairie bitch.why: The actress who played Nellie Oleson tells of her childhood fame and abuse; recommended as frank and funny.

snow.title: Snow
snow.author: Orhan Pamuk
snow.why: Pamuk's novel about a poet in a snowbound Turkish border town; recommended as a political, thoughtful literary read.

furiously happy.title: Furiously Happy
furiously happy.author: Jenny Lawson
furiously happy.why: Jenny Lawson's memoir on mental illness told with wild humour; readers call her uproariously funny.

guns germs and steel.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
guns germs and steel.author: Jared Diamond
guns germs and steel.why: Diamond's argument that geography explains the unequal spread of power; one reader calls it the best book they have read.

saving noah.title: Saving Noah
saving noah.author: Lucinda Berry
saving noah.why: Readers call it one of the most messed-up books and say it is not well written; not a real recommendation.

kristin lavransdatter.title: Kristin Lavransdatter
kristin lavransdatter.author: Sigrid Undset
kristin lavransdatter.why: Undset's trilogy of one woman's life in medieval Norway; readers recommend it as a vast, rewarding classic.

egg.title: The Egg
egg.author: Andy Weir
egg.why: A very short story about death and the nature of life; readers find it brief but excellent.

divine comedy.title: The Divine Comedy
divine comedy.author: Dante Alighieri
divine comedy.why: Dante's journey through hell, purgatory and paradise; readers recommend translations such as Ciardi's.

engine summer.title: Engine Summer
engine summer.author: John Crowley
engine summer.why: A strange, dreamlike post-apocalyptic story told by a young man; fans of Gene Wolfe often list it among favourites.

malazan book of the fallen.title: Malazan Book of the Fallen
malazan book of the fallen.author: Steven Erikson
malazan book of the fallen.why: A ten-volume epic fantasy starting with Gardens of the Moon; demanding, but fans rank it among the best.

ethan frome.title: Ethan Frome
ethan frome.author: Edith Wharton
ethan frome.why: Readers recall it as a required school read that they hated; it is not recommended.

andromeda strain.title: The Andromeda Strain
andromeda strain.author: Michael Crichton
andromeda strain.why: Scientists race to contain a deadly microbe from space; a classic techno-thriller readers still enjoy.

to sleep in a sea of stars.title: To Sleep in a Sea of Stars
to sleep in a sea of stars.author: Christopher Paolini
to sleep in a sea of stars.why: Readers call it bland and far too long; not recommended.

dragonriders of pern.title: The Dragonriders of Pern
dragonriders of pern.author: Anne McCaffrey
dragonriders of pern.why: Dragonriders defend a planet from deadly Thread; readers call it a brilliant series, starting with Dragonflight.

sentence.title: The Sentence
sentence.author: Louise Erdrich
sentence.why: A bookshop is haunted during the 2020 pandemic and the Minneapolis protests; praised and loved by Erdrich fans.

city we became.title: The City We Became
city we became.author: N. K. Jemisin
city we became.why: Readers split, one calling it a disappointment; not clearly recommended.

cage of souls.title: Cage of Souls
cage of souls.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
cage of souls.why: A convict struggles to survive in a far-future prison and a dying Earth; praised for its prose and worldbuilding.

windup girl.title: The Windup Girl
windup girl.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
windup girl.why: Comments recommend other novels and do not discuss this one.

king in yellow.title: The King in Yellow
king in yellow.author: Robert W. Chambers
king in yellow.why: A set of weird stories linked by a cursed play; a classic for Halloween reading.

likeness.title: The Likeness
likeness.author: Tana French
likeness.why: A detective goes undercover as her double in Tana French's tense Dublin mystery; readers accept the silly premise.

spy who came in from the cold.title: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
spy who came in from the cold.author: John le Carré
spy who came in from the cold.why: Le Carré's classic Cold War spy novel; readers praise its stunning twist.

down and out in paris and london.title: Down and Out in Paris and London
down and out in paris and london.author: George Orwell
down and out in paris and london.why: Orwell's account of living in poverty in two cities; excellent, essay-like nonfiction.

wild swans.title: Wild Swans
wild swans.author: Jung Chang
wild swans.why: The lives of three generations of Chinese women through the 20th century; recommended for its personal and historical sweep.

walk two moons.title: Walk Two Moons
walk two moons.author: Sharon Creech
walk two moons.why: A girl travels across the US telling the story of her friend while dealing with her mother's absence; made one reader a reader.

birnam wood.title: Birnam Wood
birnam wood.author: Eleanor Catton
birnam wood.why: Activist gardeners meet a billionaire in a thriller with unlikeable characters you cannot stop reading.

chronicles of amber.title: The chronicles of Amber
chronicles of amber.author: Roger Zelazny
chronicles of amber.why: A prince with amnesia discovers he is royalty in a parallel world; a classic fantasy series.

abarat.title: Abarat
abarat.author: Clive Barker
abarat.why: A girl is swept into a magical archipelago in Barker's illustrated young-adult fantasy trilogy.

sluts.title: The Sluts
sluts.author: Dennis Cooper
sluts.why: Readers describe it as traumatising and unsettling, not as a recommendation.

travelling cat chronicles.title: The travelling cat chronicles
travelling cat chronicles.author: Hiro Arikawa
travelling cat chronicles.why: A man and his cat travel Japan visiting old friends; a gentle, tearful story readers recommend.

gods themselves.title: The Gods Themselves
gods themselves.author: Isaac Asimov
gods themselves.why: Asimov's novel about a parallel universe's energy source and truly alien aliens; readers like its originality.

kin.title: Kin
kin.author: Tayari Jones
kin.why: Tayari Jones's story of two women from Louisiana looking for belonging and each other; readers love her work.
